feature: One drag, one undo, with Position and Size open
summary: With the Position and Size numbers open, dragging a shape and pressing Undo once puts it back exactly where it started. A number typed into a box and not sent now lands when you click the canvas, instead of being lost under a drag.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/undo-after-a-drag-with-position-and-size-open-walk.json

try.do: Draw a rectangle, switch to Select (V), and choose Position and Size from the layer's right-click menu.
Without clicking anything else, drag the rectangle somewhere new.
Press Cmd+Z again: the rectangle itself goes away, so the drag was one step.
Redo, open Position and Size, type 300 into X and do not press Return.
Press on the rectangle as if to drag it.
Press Cmd+Z once: X goes back to where it was.

evaluate: After one Cmd+Z, is the rectangle exactly where it was before the drag?
When you type 300 into X and then press on the canvas, is it right that the press only lands the 300 and does not start a drag?
Does anything about the number boxes feel different when you tab through them without typing?
rough: A press on the canvas that lands a typed number does nothing else, the same as a press that finishes typing on the canvas. So with 300 typed into X, your first press lands 300 and the drag needs a second press. Figma lands the number and starts the drag in one press.
There is no mock for this: it is an undo fix, so there is nothing to put side by side.
